title: Bonus Episode: Fake News with Chrysalis Wright, PhD

sentences.en: Hi, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Caitlin Luna, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是凯特琳·卢娜，是《心理学谈话》节目的主持人。

sentences.en: This episode was recorded live during APA 2019, our annual convention that was held in Chicago this year.
sentences.zh: 本期节目是在美国心理学会（APA）2019年年会上现场录制的，今年的年会是在芝加哥举办的。

sentences.en: I was away on maternity leave during that time, so my colleague, Dr. Vail Wright, was a guest hoSt.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在休产假，所以由我的同事韦尔·赖特博士担任客座主持人。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy the episode.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期节目。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast by the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由美国心理学会制作的播客《心理学谈话》。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Vail Wright, the Director of Research and Special Projects at APA, and I'm guest hosting this podcast today, coming to you from APA 2019 in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我是韦尔·赖特博士，美国心理学会研究与特别项目主任。今天我正在芝加哥的APA 2019年会上，担任本期节目的客座主持人。

sentences.en: Joining us today is Dr. Kerselis Wright.
sentences.zh: 今天做客我们节目的是克塞利斯·赖特博士。

sentences.en: She is the Director of Media and Migration Lab at the University of Central Florida, and we're going to be talking about fake news.
sentences.zh: 她是中佛罗里达大学媒体与移民实验室的主任，今天我们将讨论“假新闻”这个话题。

sentences.en: I mean, my goodness, fake news.
sentences.zh: 我的天，假新闻。

sentences.en: It's 2017's Word of the Year.
sentences.zh: 它是2017年的年度词汇。

sentences.en: It just made it into the Oxford English Dictionary, and it's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它刚刚被收录进《牛津英语词典》，而且随处可见。

sentences.en: So I'm hoping we can really talk about and have a dialogue about what does it mean when intentionally fabricated content is spread as fact, and why should we care about it?
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能和您深入探讨一下：当蓄意编造的内容被当作事实传播时，这意味着什么？我们为什么要关注它？

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您能参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I thought maybe one of the ways to start would be if you could tell a little bit about your background and how you kind of came to studying this type of thing,
sentences.zh: 我想开场或许可以请您简单介绍一下您的背景，以及您是如何开始研究这类课题的，

sentences.en: because I don't think a lot of psychologists necessarily go into this.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得很多心理学家未必会涉足这个领域。

sentences.en: Well, my doctorate degree is in developmental psychology, and I'm in the psychology department at the University of Central Florida.
sentences.zh: 我的博士学位是发展心理学方向的，目前在中佛罗里达大学心理学系任教。

sentences.en: And the majority of my research up until, I don't know, a couple of years ago focused on the influence of music.
sentences.zh: 在两三年前之前，我的大部分研究都集中在音乐的影响力上。

sentences.en: So most of my research focuses on the impact of entertainment media and other types of media on consumers.
sentences.zh: 所以我的大部分研究都聚焦于娱乐媒体和其他类型的媒体对消费者的影响。

sentences.en: And I started to become
sentences.zh: 而我开始对假新闻产生兴趣，

sentences.en: interested in fake news because of things I started seeing in 2015, 2016.
sentences.zh: 是因为我在2015年、2016年看到的一些现象。

sentences.en: It seemed like that term started to be thrown around a lot.
sentences.zh: 当时这个词似乎开始被频繁使用。

sentences.en: Everyone was accusing everyone else of presenting information and everything was called fake news.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在指责对方提供的信息不实，所有东西都被贴上了“假新闻”的标签。

sentences.en: But alongside that, I started to, I think we all started to see an increase in very overt prejudicial behavior that was presented to consumers through various media, avenues.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我认为我们都开始注意到，通过各种媒体渠道呈现给消费者的、非常明显的偏见行为有所增加。

sentences.en: And I wanted to know that why that was happening.
sentences.zh: 我想知道为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: So that's why I started looking at fake news.
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始研究假新闻的原因。

sentences.en: And we're all kind of consumers, right?
sentences.zh: 我们其实都是消费者，对吧？

sentences.en: Like when you're talking about it, you know,
sentences.zh: 就像您刚才提到的，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm including myself.
sentences.zh: 我也包括在内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But we're all consumers of sort of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 但我们都是某种意义上时事信息的消费者。

sentences.en: So when we're thinking about the fact that we're all consumers, our family are consumers, you know, how do we explain what is fake news?
sentences.zh: 所以当我们考虑到我们自己、我们的家人都是消费者时，我们该如何解释什么是假新闻？

sentences.en: Why is it a problem?
sentences.zh: 为什么它是个问题？

sentences.en: Well, there's, it's kind of hard to define because everyone is using the term, but the way I use it or define it in terms of a research perspective might be a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很难定义，因为每个人都在用这个词，但我从研究角度所使用或定义的含义可能略有不同。

sentences.en: So when I'm looking at fake news in terms of research, I'm looking at false, completely
sentences.zh: 所以当我从研究角度审视假新闻时，我关注的是那些完全虚假的、

sentences.en: false information that kind of perpetrates rumors, spreads misinformation with the intent of providing
sentences.zh: 散布谣言、传播错误信息，且意图向消费者提供

sentences.en: false information to consumers, which is different than say a news report that's presented from a biased perspective.
sentences.zh: 虚假信息的内容，这与那种从偏见角度出发的新闻报道是不同的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And so where does satire come into this?
sentences.zh: 那么讽刺作品在其中扮演什么角色呢？

sentences.en: Because I came across this website the other day called Taters Gonna Tate.
sentences.zh: 因为我前几天偶然发现了一个叫“Taters Gonna Tate”的网站。

sentences.en: Oh, I actually was going to talk about that today.
sentences.zh: 哦，我今天正打算聊聊这个。

sentences.en: Well, excellent.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: So, I mean, where do you fit that in?
sentences.zh: 那么，您觉得它属于哪一类？

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's a satirical website with very productive, provocative headlines that are meant to be provocative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个讽刺网站，上面有非常具有煽动性的标题，目的就是为了挑衅。

sentences.en: And it says all over, there's these disclaimers, we're satire, we're satire.
sentences.zh: 而且到处都有免责声明，写着“我们是讽刺作品，我们是讽刺作品”。

sentences.en: Well, see, that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Not everyone reads the disclaimer.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都会看免责声明。

sentences.en: I mean, you know this, not everyone reads the fine print, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，并不是每个人都会看细则，对吧？

sentences.en: Like usually we just, for instance, if you go to download an app on your phone and you have to agree to the terms and conditions, we don't actually read that.
sentences.zh: 比如通常情况下，如果你在手机上下载一个应用程序，必须同意条款和条件，我们其实并不会去读。

sentences.en: We just hit the box and say whatever and go straight to it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是勾选框，说“随便吧”，然后直接跳过。

sentences.en: So we don't read the fine print, but consumers aren't provided with the tools necessary to be able to decipher satire versus actual fake news.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不看细则，但消费者也没有被提供必要的工具来分辨讽刺作品和真正的假新闻。

sentences.en: And we saw a recent example of how misinterpreting information, how it can actually influence attitudes and even behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们最近看到了一个例子，说明误读信息如何真正影响态度甚至行为。

sentences.en: So recently there was an instance that involved two police officers in Louisiana, which is, might be how you came across the website, Taters Penitrate in the first place.
sentences.zh: 最近在路易斯安那州发生了两名警察涉事的案例，这可能就是您发现“Taters Gonna Tate”网站的原因。

sentences.en: So we had a situation where there was a police officer who was on social media.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，一名警察在社交媒体上，

sentences.en: I believe he was on Facebook and he saw a post that I believe he, he believed it was true.
sentences.zh: 我相信他是在Facebook上，看到了一篇帖子，他当时相信那是真的。

sentences.en: And the post talked about how one of our Congress women, it said something to the effect that she believed our military were overpaid for their services.
sentences.zh: 那篇帖子谈到我们的一位女国会议员，大意是说她认为我们的军人薪酬过高。

sentences.en: And so he read this article or whatever the information was on Facebook, felt really strongly about it.
sentences.zh: 于是他读了这篇文章或Facebook上的信息，对此感到非常强烈。

sentences.en: Um, and then posted a comment that was interpreted rightly as a death threat against the Congresswoman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后他发表了一条评论，被解读为针对这位女议员的死亡威胁。

sentences.en: And then another police officer liked his poSt. Both of the police officers were fired, um, especially because of the, the post that the death threat was, was a bit much.
sentences.zh: 接着另一名警察给他的帖子点了赞。两名警察都被解雇了，尤其是因为那条死亡威胁的帖子确实太过分了。

sentences.en: And that's why they, you know, they were fired from the force, but the post they were responding to was from Taters gonna
sentences.zh: 这就是他们被开除的原因，但他们回复的那篇帖子正是来自“Taters Gonna Tate”。

sentences.en: Tate.
sentences.zh: 那是网站的名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Like I, that's the name of the website, right?
sentences.zh: 他们有一个社交媒体账号，发布了那条帖子。那本意是讽刺，但显然当他们阅读时，并没有理解

sentences.en: But they have a, a social media account and they posted this poSt. It was intended to be satire, but obviously when they read it, they didn't understand
sentences.zh: 那是讽刺，反而相信那是事实信息，这导致了强烈的情绪，感到愤怒，从而引发了那条评论。

sentences.en: that it was satire, believed it was factual information and it led to, you know, strong emotions, feeling upset, which led to the posting.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，这类事情会导致我们改变态度。

sentences.en: And, you know, we know that, you know, those types of things can lead to our changing our attitudes.
sentences.zh: 我们尚不确定它能在多大程度上影响我们的实际行为。

sentences.en: We're not certain to the extent at which it can impact our actual behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们知道态度可以影响行为，但我们需要做更多的研究来连接这些点，确保路径清晰，以便我们更好地理解

sentences.en: We know attitudes can influence behaviors, but we have to do more research to connect those dots and make sure that there's a clear path so that we better understand
sentences.zh: 假新闻、错误信息和虚假信息是如何影响消费者的。

sentences.en: how fake news and false and misinformation, false information can impact consumers.
sentences.zh: 我感觉部分原因是现在的信息量实在太大，很难分辨真伪。

sentences.en: And I sort of feel like part of it is that there's just so much information out there that it can be hard to decipher which is which.
sentences.zh: 而且在我看来，今天与以往不同的是，政治人物参与其中的方式。

sentences.en: And what seems different to me about today is the way in which political figures are participating in this.
sentences.zh: 我们本应信任的领导角色人物，似乎也无法辨别这些信息。

sentences.en: People that we're supposed to trust in leadership roles just don't seem to be discerning the information either.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你不能把所有东西都称为假新闻。

sentences.en: Well, you can't call everything fake news.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为信息不符合你已有的个人观点，并不意味着它是假的。

sentences.en: Just because information doesn't necessarily align with your personal views that you have already doesn't mean that it's fake.
sentences.zh: 我们今天早上开了一个关于假新闻的会议。

sentences.en: We had a session this morning about fake news.
sentences.zh: 其中提到的一点是：仅仅因为某事是“你的真相”，并不一定意味着它是“真相”。

sentences.en: And one thing that was brought up is just because something is your truth does not necessarily mean it's the truth.
sentences.zh: 这两者是有区别的。

sentences.en: There's a difference there.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅因为人们不同意你的观点，并不意味着他们提供的信息就是假的。

sentences.en: So just because people disagree with you doesn't mean that the information that they're presenting is fake.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 或者说是错误的。

sentences.en: Or false.
sentences.zh: 我们一直被各种信息狂轰滥炸，这毫无帮助。

sentences.en: It doesn't help that we are bombarded with all of this information all of the time.
sentences.zh: 很多被认定为假新闻的信息都是通过社交媒体传播的。

sentences.en: A lot of the information that's, you know, kind of determined to be fake news is spread through social media.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个人都有社交媒体账号，包括Facebook、Twitter和YouTube。

sentences.en: Almost everyone has a social media account that includes Facebook, it includes Twitter, it includes YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以YouTube仍然被视为社交媒体平台。

sentences.en: So YouTube is still considered a social media platform.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会在上面看到一些信息。

sentences.en: Um, the information, you know, we, we see something on there.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，我们看到的信息已经符合我们原有的观点，因为呈现给我们的信息

sentences.en: Most of the time, the information that we view already agrees with, with views we have, um, because the information
sentences.zh: 是基于我们之前的点赞、点击以及所有这些行为。

sentences.en: that is presented to us is based on our previous likes and clicks and all of that.
sentences.zh: 幕后运作的任何算法本身就是有问题的，因为它并没有向我们展示任何话题的全貌。

sentences.en: Any algorithm that's working behind the scenes that in itself is problematic because it does not present us with the whole picture on any topic.
sentences.zh: 如果我们一直只看到故事的一面，我们就会开始相信这就是我们所拥有的全部信息，

sentences.en: And if we only see one side of the story or, or whatever it is all of the time, we begin to believe that that is all of the information that
sentences.zh: 但当我们遇到这些信息时，

sentences.en: we have, but we come across information.
sentences.zh: 它会让我们产生情绪。

sentences.en: It makes us feel emotional.
sentences.zh: 我们对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: We get upset about it.
sentences.zh: 我们认为其他人也应该知道这些信息。

sentences.en: We think other people should have this information.
sentences.zh: 所以我们分享它。

sentences.en: So we share it.
sentences.zh: 我们点赞。

sentences.en: We like it.
sentences.zh: 我们把它发给所有的朋友和家人。

sentences.en: We send it to all of our friends and family.
sentences.zh: 然后这个循环就持续下去了。

sentences.en: And then it just, the cycle just continues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们现在没有工具来辨别所有这些涌向我们的信息。

sentences.en: Um, we don't have the tools right now to decipher all of this information that's coming at us.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个数字世界里，我们想要立刻知道信息。

sentences.en: And we live in a, in a, like a digital world where we want to know information right now.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个问题，你可以拿出手机，用谷歌搜索。

sentences.en: So if you have a question, you can pull out your phone, you can Google it.
sentences.zh: 它会给你一个答案，而你想要的就是那一刻的信息。

sentences.en: It gives you an answer and you want the information right then.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正停下来去查看信息的来源、它来自哪里、来源的资质如何。

sentences.en: We don't really pause to look at the source of the information, where it came from, the credentials for the source.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们想要即时获取信息。

sentences.en: You know, we want our information immediately.
sentences.zh: 这也助长了这个问题。

sentences.en: And that's, that kind of feeds into the issue also.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我听过人们提到这一点，就好像，并不是人们变坏了，或者他们有党派偏见。

sentences.en: And I've heard people refer to it sort of as like, it's not that people are bad or that they're even partisan.
sentences.zh: 这更像是某种“懒惰的思考”。

sentences.en: It's more like kind of like lazy thinking.
sentences.zh: 就像我们没有付出努力去真正弄清楚我们看到的东西是否真实。

sentences.en: Like we just don't go to the effort to actually figure out whether what we're looking at is true or not.
sentences.zh: 我觉得今天早上提到的一个观点很有趣，那就是这通常是婴儿潮一代的人。

sentences.en: And I thought what was interesting about this morning that was mentioned is that it's often individuals in the baby, baby boomer generation.
sentences.zh: 他们经常转发或点赞这类假新闻。

sentences.en: They're often retweeting or re-liking these sorts of fake news.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是年轻一代的问题。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily younger generations.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的家庭中也遇到过这种情况。

sentences.en: And I come across that in my own family.
sentences.zh: 我有年长的表亲，我看到他们在Facebook上点赞或分享了某些东西，

sentences.en: I have older cousins where I see that they have liked something or shared it on their
sentences.zh: 但我一眼就能看出那不是真的。

sentences.en: Facebook and I can tell it's not true.
sentences.zh: 我想你刚才讲了一个关于你在Facebook上看到的东西的故事。

sentences.en: I think you were telling a story earlier about something you saw on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我举了一个例子，说明社交媒体是如何被用来分享假新闻或错误信息的。

sentences.en: I was given an example of how social media has been used to share fake news or false misinformation.
sentences.zh: 那是几年前我偶然看到的一篇帖子，那是一张墙的照片，大概是2016年或2017年。

sentences.en: So there was a post I came across a couple of years ago and it was a picture of a wall and it was maybe 2016, 2017.
sentences.zh: 那是一张墙的照片，上面写着大意是：墨西哥有能力保护其边境，

sentences.en: It was a picture of a wall and it said something to the effect that, you know, Mexico has the ability to protect its borders.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能？

sentences.en: Why can't we?
sentences.zh: 所以其意图是将这堵据称在墨西哥、将其与危地马拉隔开的墙，

sentences.en: So the intent was to compare this wall that is supposedly in Mexico separating it from, I believe, Guatemala
sentences.zh: 与提议在美国和墨西哥之间修建的边境墙进行比较。

sentences.en: to the proposed border wall that's been, you know, proposed to be built here between the United States and Mexico.
sentences.zh: 所以有几点：

sentences.en: So a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 是的，那确实是一张墙的照片，但它不是墨西哥或危地马拉的墙。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a picture of a wall, but it is not a picture of a wall in Mexico or Guatemala.
sentences.zh: 它不是分隔那两个地区的墙。

sentences.en: It's not a wall that separates those two areas.
sentences.zh: 相反，这是一张以色列墙的照片。

sentences.en: Instead, it's a picture of a wall that is in Israel.
sentences.zh: 它建于2013年。

sentences.en: It was built in 2013.
sentences.zh: 它与我们的政治议题毫无关系，但人们看到了它。

sentences.en: It has nothing to do with our political issue whatsoever, but people saw it.
sentences.zh: 他们分享了它，转发了它，它就像野火一样蔓延开来。

sentences.en: They shared it, retreated it, and just it spread like wildfire.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到消费者，他们相信了。

sentences.en: And you can see consumers, they believe it.
sentences.zh: 他们不去核实信息的来源，

sentences.en: They don't verify the source of the information and
sentences.zh: 他们想让每个人都看到，他们看到这个就说：看，如果墨西哥能保护他们的边境，

sentences.en: they want everyone to, you know, they see this and they're like, see if Mexico can protect their borders.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能做同样的事？

sentences.en: Why can't we do the same?
sentences.zh: 但那不是真的。

sentences.en: But that's not real.
sentences.zh: 那是假新闻。

sentences.en: That's fake news.
sentences.zh: 那是虚假信息。

sentences.en: That's false information.
sentences.zh: 这是错误信息，它在误导消费者。

sentences.en: It's misinformation and it's misleading consumers.
sentences.zh: 所以这是定义假新闻时的另一个方面。

sentences.en: So that's another thing in terms of how we define fake news.
sentences.zh: 作者制作它的意图是什么？

sentences.en: What's the intent of the author that put it together?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你告诉我某件事，说“我听说了某某某”。

sentences.en: So if you tell me something, well, I heard blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 如果那确实是你听到的，而且你真的相信它，你告诉我并不一定意味着你在传播假新闻。

sentences.en: If that's really what you heard and you really believe it, you telling me it does not necessarily mean you're sharing fake news.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但如果信息的原始作者知道那是虚假信息，并意图欺骗，那就不一样了。

sentences.en: But the author, if the original author of that information knew it was false information, intended to deceive, then that's different.
sentences.zh: 所以关键在于背后的意图。

sentences.en: So it's the intent behind it.
sentences.zh: 我们不能真的责怪每个人去分享他们在社交媒体上看到的信息。

sentences.en: We can't, we can't really blame everyone for sharing information that they come across on social media.
sentences.zh: 我们确实需要审视信息的来源，以及作者最初创作它的意图。

sentences.en: We really need to look at where the information is originating from and the author's intent in creating it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们确实需要审视信息的来源，以及作者最初创作它的意图。

sentences.en: Right, because it's the intent of the author that matters, not the re-share or the re-tweeter who might just be doing it because, like you said
sentences.zh: 没错，因为作者的意图才是关键，而不是那些转发或转推的人，他们可能只是像你刚才说的那样，

sentences.en: before, it evokes some sort of emotional reaction in them and they felt compelled to share it with others or because, you know, it reaffirms something they already believed in.
sentences.zh: 因为它引发了某种情感共鸣，让他们觉得必须分享给别人，或者是因为，你知道，这印证了他们原本就相信的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think the other thing that we were talking about this morning was this idea of wanting to be right.
sentences.zh: 我想我们今天早上讨论的另一件事是那种“想要正确”的心理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We all want to be right about everything, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都想在任何事情上都显得正确，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it ends up becoming what we call in psychology a confirmation bias, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这最终演变成了心理学上所说的“确认偏误”，对吧？

sentences.en: Is that we seek out information that confirms the beliefs we already have as opposed to seeking out information that might counter it.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们倾向于寻找那些能证实我们已有信念的信息，而不是去寻找可能反驳这些信念的信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the algorithms on social media does not help that whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 而社交媒体上的算法对此毫无帮助。

sentences.en: It makes it worse.
sentences.zh: 反而让情况更糟了。

sentences.en: So, I mean, we've hit on this a little bit, but like, what are the consequences of, you know, all this sort of misinformation and the negative intent around it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们已经稍微触及了这一点，但我想问，所有这些虚假信息及其背后的负面意图会带来什么后果呢？

sentences.en: Why should we care?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要关心？

sentences.en: Why does it matter?
sentences.zh: 这有什么意义？

sentences.en: If people start to believe false information, then they start to doubt accurate information that is accurate.
sentences.zh: 如果人们开始相信虚假信息，他们就会开始怀疑那些准确的信息。

sentences.en: So, they start to dispute scientific evidence.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们开始质疑科学证据。

sentences.en: You know, they start to fully believe this is misinformation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们开始完全相信这就是虚假信息。

sentences.en: They start to kind of fall into numerous conspiracy theories and those types of things.
sentences.zh: 他们开始陷入各种阴谋论以及类似的事情中。

sentences.en: And depending on the type of content that's in the fake news or misinformation that they're consuming, it can impact their attitudes.
sentences.zh: 根据他们所接触的假新闻或虚假信息的类型，这可能会影响他们的态度。

sentences.en: So, the research I've conducted has specifically looked at
sentences.zh: 所以，我所做的研究专门考察了

sentences.en: outcomes related to immigration attitudes, immigration policy attitudes, and Islamophobia.
sentences.zh: 与移民态度、移民政策态度以及伊斯兰恐惧症相关的结果。

sentences.en: And what I found, you know, multiple times is that people who are exposed to negative images
sentences.zh: 我多次发现，那些接触到与这些特定热点、争议话题相关的负面图像的人，

sentences.en: related to these particular, you know, hot topics, controversial topics through fake news tend to have, they develop more fake, more negative attitudes.
sentences.zh: 通过假新闻接触到这些内容，往往会产生、发展出更多、更负面的态度。

sentences.en: So, it amplifies negative attitudes that they might already have.
sentences.zh: 所以，这放大了他们原本可能就有的负面态度。

sentences.en: What we don't know is how the amplification of those negative attitudes, how it impacts behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们尚不清楚这种负面态度的放大是如何影响行为的。

sentences.en: As a researcher, I'm interested in, for instance, the recent mass shootings that took place.
sentences.zh: 作为一名研究人员，我感兴趣的是，例如，最近发生的那些大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: I'm interested in better understanding the social media profiles of, of those perpetrators.
sentences.zh: 我有兴趣更好地了解那些肇事者的社交媒体档案。

sentences.en: I want to know exactly what they were looking at in terms of social media.
sentences.zh: 我想确切地知道他们在社交媒体上看了什么。

sentences.en: What were they looking at on Facebook?
sentences.zh: 他们在 Facebook 上看了什么？

sentences.en: What were they looking at on YouTube?
sentences.zh: 他们在 YouTube 上看了什么？

sentences.en: Obviously, they had negative attitudes.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们有负面态度。

sentences.en: Something, something, something is off.
sentences.zh: 有些东西，有些东西，有些东西不对劲。

sentences.en: Something is there.
sentences.zh: 有些东西就在那里。

sentences.en: So, we all have biases and we all have, you know, our personal opinions, but there's something different when people kind of take it to the next level and cause terror.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们都有偏见，也都有个人的观点，但当人们将其提升到另一个层面并制造恐怖时，性质就完全不同了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I think sometimes it can be politically slanted, but there are other ways that fake news has had consequences, like around vaccines, right?
sentences.zh: 或者，我认为有时这可能带有政治倾向，但假新闻还有其他造成后果的方式，比如围绕疫苗的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, you know, you have these false stories around vaccines based off of false research in certain ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，围绕疫苗有一些基于虚假研究的虚假故事。

sentences.en: But when you look at the real science, of course, it tells a different story.
sentences.zh: 但当你审视真正的科学时，当然，它讲述的是另一个故事。

sentences.en: But at this point, you almost can't rewind the clock.
sentences.zh: 但在这一点上，你几乎无法让时光倒流。

sentences.en: Like once people start to believe something and they have lost trust in institutions, then what do we do?
sentences.zh: 一旦人们开始相信某件事，并且对机构失去了信任，那我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: We need to better arm our consumers.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更好地武装我们的消费者。

sentences.en: We need to make sure that they are better educated in terms of media literacy.
sentences.zh: 我们需要确保他们在媒体素养方面受到更好的教育。

sentences.en: We need to make sure that they understand that sometimes, not all the time, but sometimes authors who put out information are trying to trick them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要确保他们明白，有时——不是总是，但有时——发布信息的作者是在试图欺骗他们。

sentences.en: We need to arm them so that they're aware of these facts, that it's not fake news.
sentences.zh: 我们需要武装他们，让他们意识到这些事实，让他们知道这不是假新闻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fake news is not, you know, that they're aware of these facts and that they can better protect themselves.
sentences.zh: 假新闻不是，你知道，他们需要意识到这些事实，这样他们才能更好地保护自己。

sentences.en: We need to make sure that consumers know how, because identifying information that's false is very hard.
sentences.zh: 我们需要确保消费者知道该怎么做，因为识别虚假信息非常困难。

sentences.en: It's difficult.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: So, we need to make sure that consumers know how to pause, check the source of the information.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要确保消费者知道如何停下来，检查信息的来源。

sentences.en: Where is it coming from?
sentences.zh: 它来自哪里？

sentences.en: If they can't find the source, just leave it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们找不到来源，那就别管它。

sentences.en: Because if you're not able to verify the source of the information,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你无法核实信息来源，

sentences.en: I would just consider it false information and not even go there.
sentences.zh: 我建议直接将其视为虚假信息，根本不要去理会。

sentences.en: But consumers also need to kind of, especially in terms of social media, pause when they see something that makes them emotional, whether it's a negative or positive emotion.
sentences.zh: 但消费者也需要，特别是在社交媒体方面，当他们看到让自己产生情绪的东西时，无论是负面还是正面情绪，都要停下来。

sentences.en: Pause for a minute, think about what is it about this piece of information that's got me upset?
sentences.zh: 停下来想一分钟，这条信息里有什么让我心烦意乱的地方？

sentences.en: Why do I want to share it with other people?
sentences.zh: 为什么我想把它分享给别人？

sentences.en: And make sure that they understand that, you know, if you share it, then to a certain extent, you're somewhat, you know, responsible for spreading false information.
sentences.zh: 并确保他们明白，你知道，如果你分享了它，那么在某种程度上，你也要对传播虚假信息负责。

sentences.en: So, if we can better arm our consumers and help them to be better able to identify false information, I think it will help a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们能更好地武装我们的消费者，帮助他们更好地识别虚假信息，我想会有所帮助。

sentences.en: But once that trust is gone, we have to work to get it back.
sentences.zh: 但一旦信任消失，我们就必须努力去重建它。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I think, like you said, it can be really challenging because
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如你所说，这可能真的很有挑战性，因为

sentences.en: the producers of the false information are using visuals and these provocative headlines and trying to go for shock, right?
sentences.zh: 虚假信息的制造者正在使用视觉效果和这些挑衅性的标题，试图制造冲击力，对吧？

sentences.en: So that it gets you worked up and it gets you reactionary instead of pausing.
sentences.zh: 这样会让你情绪激动，让你产生反应，而不是停下来思考。

sentences.en: And that's exactly why false news and fake news is so memorable, why it's persistent.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么假新闻如此令人印象深刻，为什么它如此持久的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, there's been research that has shown that even if you tell people, okay, the information that you just shared is false, here is proof that it's false.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有研究表明，即使你告诉人们，好吧，你刚才分享的信息是假的，这里有证据证明它是假的。

sentences.en: Here's a scientific study that proves the information you just told me is false.
sentences.zh: 这是一项证明你刚才告诉我的信息是假的科学研究。

sentences.en: They still believe it because of how shocking it is, because of how sensational it is.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然相信它，因为它太令人震惊了，因为它太耸人听闻了。

sentences.en: It has more of an effect than real information.
sentences.zh: 它比真实信息更有影响力。

sentences.en: So that, that in itself is part of the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以，这本身就是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: People need to understand, if you see a headline that just seems completely out of this world, completely unrealistic, it probably is.
sentences.zh: 人们需要明白，如果你看到的标题看起来完全不可思议、完全不现实，那它很可能就是假的。

sentences.en: You know, the headlines should just be from more hard news or reputable news sources, they tend to just relay the facts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，标题应该来自更严肃的新闻或知名新闻来源，它们往往只是陈述事实。

sentences.en: If you see something that is shocking, whether it's images, the headline itself, the way that the information is shared,
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一些令人震惊的东西，无论是图片、标题本身，还是信息分享的方式，

sentences.en: then there's a reason for that, you know, that it makes it more memorable, but it doesn't make it true.
sentences.zh: 那么这背后是有原因的，你知道，这让它更容易被记住，但这并不代表它是真的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, and I think, you know, in the wake of sort of this phenomenon, you, some
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为，在这种现象出现之后，一些

sentences.en: social media companies have tried to take counter measures, right?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体公司已经尝试采取反制措施，对吧？

sentences.en: Sort of labeling things as false or putting tags on them.
sentences.zh: 比如给内容贴上虚假标签或标记。

sentences.en: Seems like the research is pretty mixed on whether or not that's effective.
sentences.zh: 看起来关于这是否有效，研究结果相当不一致。

sentences.en: Is that an accurate read?
sentences.zh: 这种解读准确吗？

sentences.en: Well, for one, when YouTube did that, it totally messed up one of my research studies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，当 YouTube 这样做时，它彻底搞砸了我的一个研究项目。

sentences.en: So I'm not, so you're not a fan.
sentences.zh: 所以我不，所以你不是粉丝。

sentences.en: Well, I think we have to be aware of where the, who's that, who's to blame, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们必须意识到，谁该为此负责，对吧？

sentences.en: Who's, who's responsible for the information?
sentences.zh: 谁，谁该对这些信息负责？

sentences.en: So you have social media platforms that don't want to be responsible for the sharing of misinformation that could potentially lead to whatever negative consequences.
sentences.zh: 所以你有社交媒体平台，它们不想为传播可能导致任何负面后果的虚假信息负责。

sentences.en: And I think that's why they have started to step in and start to block content and remove stuff like the Alex Jones YouTube channel, which is, I was using that as
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么他们开始介入，开始屏蔽内容并删除像 Alex Jones 的 YouTube 频道这样的东西，我当时正把它用作

sentences.en: a fake news example in a research study.
sentences.zh: 研究中的一个假新闻案例。

sentences.en: So I had to stop data collection altogether and kind of use what I already had.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不完全停止数据收集，只能使用我现有的数据。

sentences.en: So we'll see how that goes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看看结果会怎样。

sentences.en: But they did it because they don't want to be responsible for the information.
sentences.zh: 但他们这样做是因为他们不想对这些信息负责。

sentences.en: So, but what we're looking at is not, it is not a technological problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所看到的并不是一个技术问题。

sentences.en: It is not a social media problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个社交媒体问题。

sentences.en: It is a people problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人的问题。

sentences.en: Our, you know, looking for information that already confirms what we believe, being drawn to information that is shocking, sensational,
sentences.zh: 我们，你知道，寻找能证实我们已有信念的信息，被那些令人震惊、耸人听闻的信息所吸引，

sentences.en: that causes us to be emotional, wanting to tell every, you know, everyone information that we think we know.
sentences.zh: 这让我们产生情绪，想要告诉每个人，你知道，我们认为我们知道的信息。

sentences.en: Those are areas that are problematic, that are kind of increasing the spread of social media, you know, the fake news through social media.
sentences.zh: 这些都是有问题的地方，它们在某种程度上增加了社交媒体上假新闻的传播。

sentences.en: So we have to be very cautious about taking stuff down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在删除内容时必须非常谨慎。

sentences.en: Who makes the decision to take it down?
sentences.zh: 谁来决定删除它？

sentences.en: You know, are they biased in some way?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是否有某种偏见？

sentences.en: So is it their bias that is leading them to want to remove content?
sentences.zh: 那么，是他们的偏见导致他们想要删除内容吗？

sentences.en: Or do they know for sure if they've done their fact checking and they know for sure that it's false information?
sentences.zh: 还是他们确实进行了事实核查，并确定这确实是虚假信息？

sentences.en: So it becomes kind of sticky because, you know, we have the right to free the free speech, but that doesn't mean we have the right
sentences.zh: 所以这变得有点棘手，因为，你知道，我们有言论自由的权利，但这并不意味着我们有权利

sentences.en: for hate speech, for instance, or free speech without consequences.
sentences.zh: 发表仇恨言论，或者发表不需要承担后果的言论。

sentences.en: So there's a line and we have to, as a society, kind of figure out exactly where that is and what's protected and what isn't.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一条界线，作为一个社会，我们必须弄清楚这条界线到底在哪里，什么受到保护，什么不受保护。

sentences.en: Do we have an administration that can do that?
sentences.zh: 我们有能做到这一点的政府吗？

sentences.en: I think something like that has to be a bipartisan decision.
sentences.zh: 我认为这样的事情必须是一个两党共同的决定。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: That's an excellent bipartisan decision.
sentences.zh: 那是一个极好的两党共同决定。

sentences.en: So both sides of the aisle have to come together to kind of solve this, help solve this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以两党必须共同努力来解决这个问题，帮助解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And one thing we have to do is quit calling everything fake news.
sentences.zh: 我们必须做的一件事就是停止把一切都称为假新闻。

sentences.en: Just because I tell you something is fake news doesn't mean that it's fake.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我告诉你某件事是假新闻，并不意味着它就是假的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: You know, so we have to stop throwing that term around as if, I mean, we hear it every day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以我们必须停止到处乱用这个词，我的意思是，我们每天都能听到它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We have to stop that and pay attention and make sure that what we're sharing is factual information, you know, regardless of who it is.
sentences.zh: 我们必须停止这样做，要多加注意，确保我们分享的是事实信息，你知道，无论它是来自谁。

sentences.en: And just stay off Twitter.
sentences.zh: 还有，别再上 Twitter 了。

sentences.en: She says after I've already tweeted out that I am here right now doing this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 她说这话的时候，我已经发推说我正坐在这里录制这个播客。

sentences.en: You know, one of the things you brought up earlier that made me think was around Alex Jones, his YouTube channel.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你之前提到的关于 Alex Jones 和他的 YouTube 频道的事情让我思考。

sentences.en: And I think one of the other motives around spreading misinformation is for profit.
sentences.zh: 我认为传播虚假信息的另一个动机是为了利益。

sentences.en: So a lot of his, if you ever watch his work is really around selling a lot of products that he has.
sentences.zh: 所以他很多，如果你看过他的作品，其实都是为了推销他拥有的很多产品。

sentences.en: And he gets people to click on his stuff and come to his page because he's being sensationalist and loud.
sentences.zh: 他让人点击他的东西并来到他的页面，因为他耸人听闻且大声喧哗。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, he's really trying to sell you something.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，他真的只是想卖给你东西。

sentences.en: How, what role do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: That sort of selling the profit component of sort of behind all of this spread, it'd be an intent of spreading.
sentences.zh: 那种销售、那种利润成分，是所有这些传播背后的意图吗？

sentences.en: Well, we see the for profit issue in hard news or mainstream news.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在严肃新闻或主流新闻中也看到了这种以营利为目的的问题。

sentences.en: Also, everything is, is for profit, right?
sentences.zh: 同样，一切都是为了营利，对吧？

sentences.en: So, um, even in mainstream traditional news outlets, they're, they have commercials that they're trying to sell you in between news breaks and the way they
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，即使在主流传统新闻媒体中，他们也有商业广告，试图在新闻间隙卖给你东西，而且他们

sentences.en: present information is done in such a way where they want you as a consumer to watch their show rather than the other one so that they can make more money.
sentences.zh: 呈现信息的方式，是希望你作为消费者观看他们的节目，而不是别人的，这样他们才能赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: So it kind of boils down to profit, regardless of if it's hard news or fake news.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底还是为了利润，不管它是严肃新闻还是假新闻。

sentences.en: Um, fake news gets a little bit more tricky because, um, for instance, yes, Alex Jones was selling products and that type of stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，假新闻有点棘手，因为，嗯，例如，是的，Alex Jones 在卖产品之类的东西。

sentences.en: Um, but not everyone who creates fake news is getting a profit in that way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但并不是每个制造假新闻的人都是以那种方式获利的。

sentences.en: It doesn't always have to be a monetary profit.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非要是金钱利益。

sentences.en: Um, it could be, well, I want a lot of people to vote this particular way, so I'm going to create some sensational information and put it out there to try to
sentences.zh: 嗯，它可能是，好吧，我想让很多人以这种特定的方式投票，所以我打算制造一些耸人听闻的信息并发布出去，试图

sentences.en: convince people to do what I want them to do.
sentences.zh: 说服人们做我想要他们做的事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: To influence them in some way.
sentences.zh: 以某种方式影响他们。

sentences.en: In some way.
sentences.zh: 以某种方式。

sentences.en: It doesn't necessarily have to be a monetary issue.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非要是金钱问题。

sentences.en: So, you know, for our listeners, other than being more media literate or media savvy, what can people do to help figure out what news is legitimate and what news might not be?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，对于我们的听众来说，除了提高媒体素养或媒体敏锐度之外，人们还能做些什么来帮助判断哪些新闻是合法的，哪些可能不是？

sentences.en: Um, well, you can fact check the news.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以核实新闻的事实。

sentences.en: That would be helpful.
sentences.zh: 那会有帮助。

sentences.en: Um, but let's say I don't have time to fact check the news.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但假设我没有时间核实新闻。

sentences.en: Then you shouldn't be reading.
sentences.zh: 那你就别读了。

sentences.en: Then don't read it.
sentences.zh: 那就别读它。

sentences.en: Um, because we have to be wise consumers, you know, we live in an age where we want everything right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我们必须成为明智的消费者，你知道，我们生活在一个想要立刻得到一切的时代。

sentences.en: We want everything instant.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一切即时呈现。

sentences.en: We don't really want to, we don't have time to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不想，我们没有时间去做那些事。

sentences.en: We're all working.
sentences.zh: 我们都在工作。

sentences.en: Everyone is busy.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很忙。

sentences.en: Um, but we need to make the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我们需要挤出时间。

sentences.en: If we want accurate information, we have to work to get it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想要准确的信息，就必须付出努力去获取。

sentences.en: And one of the best things about social media and the internet is that we have all of the information we could possibly think of at our fingertips.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体和互联网最棒的一点在于，我们触手可及就能获得所有能想到的信息。

sentences.en: But it's how we're using those tools that starts to become problematic.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于我们使用这些工具的方式开始变得有问题了。

sentences.en: Um, because people are creating information that's not real, it's fake, it's false.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为人们正在制造虚假、不真实的信息。

sentences.en: Um, and the more you spread it, the more people start to believe it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你传播得越多，人们就越开始相信它。

sentences.en: So we need to make sure that we're checking the source and we have to engage in some type of self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要确保核实来源，并且必须进行某种程度的自我反思。

sentences.en: Why is this information important to me?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些信息对我来说很重要？

sentences.en: How does it make me feel?
sentences.zh: 它让我有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Why do I want to share it?
sentences.zh: 我为什么想分享它？

sentences.en: And we need to pause and really kind of consider those things before we share information we come across on social media, before we tell our friends and family.
sentences.zh: 在分享我们在社交媒体上看到的信息，或者告诉亲朋好友之前，我们需要停下来，真正地考虑这些问题。

sentences.en: Um, why is it important to us?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么它对我们很重要？

sentences.en: I also thought it was interesting this morning talking about how we only maybe receive half of the story.
sentences.zh: 今天早上讨论到我们可能只接收到了一半的故事，我觉得这一点也很有趣。

sentences.en: And so what that made me think about is can we be more inquisitive, right, as individuals?
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，作为个人，我们能否更加好奇一点呢？

sentences.en: Can we ask ourselves, okay,
sentences.zh: 我们能否问问自己，好吧，

sentences.en: I've heard this part of the story.
sentences.zh: 我听到了故事的这一部分。

sentences.en: Is there more?
sentences.zh: 还有更多内容吗？

sentences.en: What's the and?
sentences.zh: 剩下的部分是什么？

sentences.en: There's always more, right?
sentences.zh: 总是有更多内容，对吧？

sentences.en: There's always more.
sentences.zh: 总是有更多内容。

sentences.en: Um, and we do get half the story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实只得到了故事的一半。

sentences.en: So even from, um, like mainstream news sources, CNN and Fox, those are both of those avenues are very biased.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是像CNN和福克斯新闻这样的主流新闻来源，这两个渠道也都是非常有偏见的。

sentences.en: So on the way here, um, I was kind of flipping back and forth between how Fox News and how CNN was discussing the mass shootings that recently took
sentences.zh: 所以在来这里的路上，我一直在切换频道，看福克斯新闻和CNN是如何讨论最近发生的那些大规模枪击事件的，

sentences.en: place and, um, the president's tweets and rhetoric and those types of things that have happened prior to and shortly after.
sentences.zh: 以及总统的推文、言论，还有那些在事件发生前和发生后不久所发生的事情。

sentences.en: And both of those sources are presenting the same story, right?
sentences.zh: 这两个来源呈现的都是同一个故事，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So both of them have facts in there, but the way they're describing it, the slant they're put on it, the, and all of that is very biased.
sentences.zh: 所以它们都有事实依据，但它们描述的方式、所持的立场，以及所有这些，都是非常有偏见的。

sentences.en: So if you're only watching say CNN, you only get half the story.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你只看CNN，你只得到了故事的一半。

sentences.en: Um, or if you're only watching Fox, you're only getting half the story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者如果你只看福克斯，你也只得到了故事的一半。

sentences.en: We, we need to make sure that we're getting our information from multiple sources, engaging in fact checking, looking, doing our own research.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们需要确保从多个来源获取信息，进行事实核查，去寻找，去做我们自己的研究。

sentences.en: No one wants to do it, but you have to do it if you're going to be a responsible consumer.
sentences.zh: 没人想做这些，但如果你想成为一个负责任的消费者，你就必须去做。

sentences.en: You know, at some point it's our responsibility to make sure that what we believe as truth for ourselves is actually the truth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在某种程度上，确保我们自己所相信的真相确实是真相，是我们的责任。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is there a reason to feel hopeful?
sentences.zh: 有理由感到充满希望吗？

sentences.en: There's always reasons to be hopeful because we can always make a change.
sentences.zh: 总是有理由充满希望，因为我们总能做出改变。

sentences.en: That's one of the things that's great about being people is if you see something that you don't like the way things are
sentences.zh: 作为人类，最棒的一点就是，如果你看到事情的发展方向让你不满意，

sentences.en: going, then you can put in effort and energy to make a change.
sentences.zh: 那么你就可以投入精力和努力去做出改变。

sentences.en: Um, and we have, as a society, we have to all come together and decide that that's something that we want to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为一个社会，我们必须团结一致，决定这就是我们想要做的事情。

sentences.en: If, if we don't, then we're just going to see this type of thing just progress and probably snowball and just continuously get worse.
sentences.zh: 如果，如果我们不这样做，那么我们只会看到这种事情不断发展，可能会像滚雪球一样，持续恶化。

sentences.en: But if as a society, we come together and say, okay, we want to make sure that the information that we are getting is accurate, true information, then we can make
sentences.zh: 但如果作为一个社会，我们团结起来说，好吧，我们想要确保我们获取的信息是准确、真实的信息，那么我们就能确保

sentences.en: sure that that happens.
sentences.zh: 这一点能够实现。

sentences.en: So it's on us.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于我们。

sentences.en: On consumers, yes.
sentences.zh: 取决于消费者，是的。

sentences.en: On consumers.
sentences.zh: 取决于消费者。

sentences.en: And, and probably some people in charge.
sentences.zh: 还有，可能还有一些负责人的人。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: That, if we're passing laws, um, and that type of thing, it really has to be something that's bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要通过法律，嗯，诸如此类的事情，它真的必须是两党共同支持的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Um, they have to be able to put their political differences aside and figure out a way to work, work together.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们必须能够放下政治分歧，找到一种共同合作的方法。

sentences.en: Like you could be Democrat, I could be Republican.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以是民主党人，我也可以是共和党人。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。

sentences.en: You have to be able to put your differences aside and work together, um, to benefit society as a whole.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够放下分歧，共同努力，嗯，造福整个社会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that we, and you know, as we had talked, society benefits from facts.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们，你知道，正如我们所谈到的，社会受益于事实。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Factual information is helpful.
sentences.zh: 事实信息是有帮助的。

sentences.en: So that then you can make informed decisions about what you do.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以对自己的行为做出明智的决定。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for being here today.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你今天来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: I really want to thank Dr. Wright for sharing your expertise on this really timely and important topic.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常感谢赖特博士分享你在这一非常及时且重要的话题上的专业见解。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢今天听到的内容，欢迎随时通过 speakingofpsychology@apa.org 给我们发送你的想法和建议。

sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣收听我们更多的播客，可以在 iTunes、Stitcher 或任何你获取播客的地方找到它们。

sentences.en: They're also available on our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 它们也可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上找到。

sentences.zh: 嗯，我是瓦尔·赖特博士。

sentences.en: It's really been a pleasure to, uh, guest host this podcaSt. I want to thank all our listeners and everybody take care.
sentences.zh: 能担任这个播客的客座主持真是我的荣幸。我想感谢所有的听众，祝大家一切顺利。
